For C=0 along nonzero iterates put t=a*tau, q=(1+2t)^(-1/2); summing all post-reversal increments gives phi_infty/phi0=(2q^2+3q-1)/(2q), so the first negative branch remains negative at every finite n iff t >= (11+3*sqrt(17))/4. This is NOT a global theorem on later crossings. For a=phi0=1,tau=100 and 0<C<=1/2, the first state is <-17/3, subsequent r contracts by >10 and total post-first displacement is <5/3, closing all-step phi_n<-4 and phi_infty<-4 rigorously. Independent Decimal finite iterates at C=0.0001,0.1,0.5, plus direct algebraic checks of the recurrence, corroborate only these analytic bounds. C=0 is singular exactly at phi=0 and is restricted accordingly; C>0 is nonsingular.
